status: Source-fit authoring design submitted for repository review; no learner attainment or staging publication.

source.treatment: Codes-only; official expectation wording stays in the private source packet.

actions: Choose a purpose and actual intended audience with teacher support, then explain the resulting form, vocabulary, tone and organisation choices. Compare an informal peer invitation with a polite teacher information note and clear instructions for a younger reader. Discussion may use the learner’s stronger language to isolate planning decisions; the resulting texts and intended messages must be in French. Re-express the same familiar informative content for a peer and a younger reader, changing real vocabulary or sentence length to isolate the audience decision rather than only change a greeting.

Write original appropriate short French texts across the selected forms. Models illustrate structure; copying them unchanged is not independent production. Keep the intended invitation’s greeting/message/closing, an information text’s topic/development/conclusion and the recipe’s title/ingredient list/ordered instructions. Choose and explain relevant basic structural/stylistic features rather than merely change fonts.

For the whole unchanged audience-writing claim, develop and organise content coherently from introduction through development to an appropriate conclusion/closing, maintaining consistent style for the intended reader. Re-read the draft to check those decisions and revise a real ambiguity or add genuinely useful information after audience feedback.

For the whole French written-form claim, study the explicit familiar corpus separately, then retrieve taught exact spellings and accents after a delay without a written model and use selected words in a changed meaningful message. Correct copying, English spelling or fluent French speech alone does not establish this knowledge. These checks preserve the new claim; they are not extra universal Ontario word-count/delay standards.

Transfer to a new audience/purpose with familiar French content. Choose and produce a changed appropriate form and explain the effect of a real language/structure choice. A sophisticated English essay cannot substitute for an intelligible short French message.
purpose-forms-and-production.positive: Actually produces varied French texts with supported audience/purpose decisions, appropriate basic form features and coherent development/closing; retained French written forms are separately evidenced.
nearMiss: Copies a French model without creating a message.
Labels an audience but writes the same inappropriate content/style for everyone.
Infers French spelling from an English score.

actions: Actually use all four writing modes: hear a teacher model planning a short French note; jointly gather/select key words and ideas in shared writing; make a guided plan with teacher/peer prompts; then independently plan a changed familiar-topic text. Use more than one pre-writing resource/strategy, such as a picture stimulus, a short familiar reading, a word organiser and partner discussion. Each mode must occur; a list of their names does not satisfy the condition.

For the unchanged whole planning/hard-prerequisite operations, orally rehearse complete French sentences and note key words before composing. Also plan a short familiar three-part story from the original book characters, with beginning/middle/end and a changed event. Check the sentence/fragment distinction, adding detail, partner rehearsal and the complete writing-process concept vocabulary separately. This supplementary whole-claim evidence does not turn every source example into a separate topic.

Plan and produce an original draft following an actual provided invitation, information or instruction model. Make a real content revision after teacher and peer questions—add needed detail, remove an irrelevant item or clarify/reorder content. Show the change and its effect, rather than assert that revision happened. A perfect first draft does not require planted errors; an audience’s genuine new question can motivate meaningful clarification.

Improve actual written French with a few taught conventions: exact familiar words/accents, capitals/sentence punctuation and consistent intended time using familiar verb forms. Use references and teacher support while editing as appropriate. Separately preserve the new written-form claim’s independent delayed retrieval check; a dictionary-assisted edit alone is not evidence of retention.

Use the explicitly labelled teacher practice draft for diagnosis before reviewing own work: «lina va a l'ecole» can be improved to «Lina va à l'école.» after meaning/model instruction. For tense consistency, the stated intended event is that Lina AND Sam are playing now; compare the teacher draft «En ce moment, Lina joue. Sam jouera avec elle.» with the supplied familiar present-form model and correct the unintended future meaning. A tense change in a genuinely different-time account is not automatically an error. These are authored practice drafts, not fabricated learner mistakes.

Produce a polished version using a larger heading and selective emphasis that serve the purpose; do not make every word bold. For the unchanged publication claim, type the selected French text in a digital tool and read own writing aloud clearly to teacher/peers. A classroom draft/print/local display is enough for this design; no external account or real message sending is required.

Transfer through the same process with changed familiar content and form. Check the written message’s actual meaning, revised content, few conventions and presentation; visible steps or a neat copied page alone do not establish the whole source.
planning-through-publication.positive: Carries out all stages, actual modelled/shared/guided/independent pre-writing, model-based drafting, supported revision, a few actual French convention improvements and effective presentation/publication.
nearMiss: Only copies a final polished model.
Calls a spelling correction the entire content-revision process.
Marks any mixed past/present wording wrong without checking intended time.

actions: Discuss with teacher AND peer a few actual strategies used before, during and after writing. Point to the plan, draft and final work so that a strategy statement refers to a real writing action. A generic reading/speaking self-rating is insufficient.

Identify a supported writing strength and a less secure operation, compare planned and actual work and explain one specific process difference. Honest absence of confusion is acceptable; do not invent a deficit or require a particular feeling.

Choose a realistic writing goal with a timeframe, plan at least three manageable steps, record attempts and review/adjust the approach. For example, across the next three appropriate writing attempts, practise retrieving taught accented forms, use them in a message and compare later attempts with the intended forms. Select the learner’s actual need rather than impose this example on everyone.

Retain the complete existing goal/task-step/growth/mistake readiness checks using genuine available learning examples: acknowledge specific progress, distinguish improved-with-practice beliefs from fixed inability, and describe a real mistake/retry/learning experience. No frustration or manufactured error is required.
Apply the chosen next strategy to another appropriate French writing task and explain what helped or what should change next. The next attempt, not a promise alone, checks monitoring and transfer.
writing-strategy-review.positive: Explains actual before/during/after writing strategies with teacher and peer, identifies evidenced strengths/next needs and carries out monitored realistic improvement steps.
nearMiss: Repeats the listening reflection with no writing example.
Sets an unmonitored vague goal such as write better.

resources.scope: Learners produce changed meaningful messages rather than merely copy these models. Recipe writing does not require preparing food. Arrange actual teacher/peer opportunities and a digital writing tool before use; no delivered classroom trial or software lesson is claimed.

wholeClaimBoundaries: Seven shared topics retain exact authored claims and guides; one attributed community-ID adaptation addresses independent French written lexical knowledge, not another writing-process clone.
Actual French convention and message evidence remains required; general English skills do not automatically certify French form knowledge.
A few written conventions are selected concretely; the source’s illustrative adjective/verb/pronoun lists are not treated as an exhaustive mandatory French grammar inventory.

The15-card pre-correction hard closure was read completely and has no current teaching guides. The two broader craft-terminology gates are separately corrected; all retained process-vocabulary, sentence, feedback and goal-setting operations remain explicit. One new low-confidence written-form guide is an untested proposal, not efficacy evidence. No learner posterior is copied or reset.
This adds eight of44CoreGrade4records after the prior24designs; the twelve cultural/intercultural records and other primary FSL grades/programmes remain in scope.

Original proposed community card is unaccepted; no current topic meaning or learner claim is overwritten.

reuseComparison.mismatch: Spoken comprehension and delayed oral use do not establish retrieval of written French letters/accents. A learner can say monsieur correctly but write monsie.
Recognising a printed word and unusual correspondence does not establish spelling it without the written choice.

reuseComparison.candidate: mt_6W5zzDIGZH dictionary spelling check / mt_I65kFjWwnF proofreading
reuseComparison.mismatch: Reference use and revision strategies can succeed without retaining the specific French written form after the reference is removed.
English word-list or grapheme mastery does not establish monsieur/femme/temps or French accents. No broader generic procedural spelling clone is proposed.

Complete current card/evidence/prompt target English exception spellings and all seven weekday names. Spelling said/were/come and those weekdays does not establish retained French monsieur/école/à; do not silently generalise this existing claim.

Complete sentence-dictation card includes taught GPC/rule application and sentence punctuation and can succeed immediately. It does not independently establish delayed French lexical spelling retrieval and changed-message reuse.

newClaimSourceConditionLimit: The delayed/no-model check qualifies this particular written-form claim; the official D2.3 source does not prescribe a universal delay or word-count minimum. Actual improvement/conventions/presentation require the separate complete writing protocol.

before.reason: Identifying audience, purpose, form, tone, and register before writing requires all these as named vocabulary

after.reason: Writing-craft vocabulary supports explaining form and tone choices; identifying audience and purpose, choosing an appropriate form and adjusting vocabulary, sentence length and formality do not require the complete rhetoric, voice, cohesion and style terminology inventory.

before.reason: Producing coherent writing for task/purpose/audience requires these as precise, understood concepts

after.reason: Writing-craft vocabulary supports discussing coherent writing; deliberately matching task, purpose and audience, organising development and reviewing consistent style do not require the complete rhetoric, voice, cohesion and style terminology inventory.

positiveWholeTargetWitnesses: A learner explicitly chooses an informal peer note versus a polite teacher information note, explains audience/purpose/form and a real tone/wording change, and adjusts a message for a younger reader, without knowing every rhetoric/voice/cohesion term.

A learner produces and reviews coherent writing with an introduction, developed relevant content and an appropriate conclusion, checks consistent style for its actual audience and explains choices, without mastering the entire writing-craft terminology inventory.
dependencyReview.limit: Both witnesses apply within English as well as French. Preserve all actual target decisions, explanations, coherent development and review; copying a model or changing a greeting alone fails.

reviewNotes: Independent full eight-source, selected-card and hard-closure review found the complete writing duties accounted for. Delayed written-form retrieval is separate from the official source minimum; the tense task states the intended same-time event. Broader writing-craft terminology gates were independently challenged using whole-target positive witnesses.
